evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Compliant verification results are valid for 7 days.
evidence.answer: Compliant brand verification results are valid for 7 days; if not published in that window, re-verification is required.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Branding modifications are not permitted while verification is in progress.
evidence.answer: Branding changes cannot be made while brand verification is in progress; the verification must be canceled first.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.
evidence.answer: A published branding status is required before a data access (sensitive scope) verification request can be made.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Google Workspace organization administrators might restrict access to sensitive scopes to prevent access by OAuth client IDs that the organization doesn't explicitly mark as trusted.
evidence.answer: Google Workspace administrators may restrict access to sensitive scopes for OAuth client IDs their organization has not marked as trusted.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Organization administrators are the only accounts that can add the app to an allowlist for use within their domains.
evidence.answer: For domain-wide installs, organization administrators are the only accounts that can add the app to an allowlist for use within their domains.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console . Use a Google Account that's associated with your API Console project as an Owner or an Editor.
evidence.answer: The developer must verify ownership of the project's authorized domains in Google Search Console, using a Google Account that is an Owner or Editor on the project.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: hosted within the same domain as your application's home page
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must be hosted within the same domain as the application's home page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Use the Add or remove scopes button to declare all scopes requested by your app.
evidence.answer: Scopes are declared in the Cloud Console's Data Access page, and the Add or remove scopes button is used to declare all scopes requested by the app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: For example, a project can contain one or more OAuth clients, configure APIs for use by those clients, and configure an OAuth consent screen that's shown to users before they authorize access to your app.
evidence.answer: A Cloud Console project can contain one or more OAuth clients and configure the OAuth consent screen shown before users authorize the app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If your app also requires verification for sensitive or restricted scopes, navigate to the OAuth Verification Center to track your Data access status and provide any additional information requested, such as a demonstration video.
evidence.answer: Verification is requested from the Cloud Console OAuth Branding page, then the OAuth Verification Center is used to track data access status.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: One use case is if you are the only user of your app or if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to you.
evidence.answer: Exemption applies only where the app is used by a limited number of personally known users; the page gives no specific number.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Make sure all branding information on the OAuth consent screen, such as the app name, support email, home page URI, privacy policy URI, etc., accurately represents the app's identity.
evidence.answer: Branding requirements of the associated APIs or product must be complied with, and branding info must accurately represent the app's identity.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Help Scout uses OAuth 2.0 but publishes no discrete scopes — access is governed by the grant itself (e.g. client-credentials or role-based authorization) rather than per-scope consent.
evidence.answer: Per this third-party scope catalog, Help Scout publishes no discrete OAuth scopes, so there is no scope tier list that would trigger extra review; this is not confirmed against Help Scout's official docs.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations.
evidence.answer: API access requires a paid Help Scout plan (the Free plan excludes API and integrations); Standard, Plus and Pro differ in rate limits and reporting endpoint access.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Your customers don't have access to log in to Help Scout, and you can provide support for as many customers as you'd like on each plan.
evidence.answer: Plans are billed per User per month for team members; end customers are not billed and need no Help Scout login, so no per-customer fee applies on this page.
